cards.hint: Think of the early estimate later judged too small.
cards.quote: Lord Kelvin’s cooling-magma calculations yielded an age of 20–400 million years.
cards.stem: What age for Earth did the cooling magma calculation produce?

cards.hint: Picture a stack with the earliest layer at the base.
options: older rocks are on the bottom and younger rocks are on the top
sedimentary layers are deposited in horizontal layers
something that cuts across a boundary must be younger
cards.quote: The law of superposition says that older rocks are on the bottom and younger rocks are on the top.
cards.stem: How are older and younger rocks arranged in undisturbed layers?

cards.hint: Focus on how much parent material changes.
options: half of the number of original, or parent, isotopes to decay
all parent isotopes vanish in a single instant
daughter isotopes change back into parent isotopes
stable rock layers turn to molten magma again
cards.quote: A half-life is the length of time it takes for half of the number of original, or parent, isotopes to decay to a stable daughter isotope.
cards.stem: What happens during a single half-life span?

cards.hint: Recall the meteorite age linked to the age of Earth.
cards.quote: used lead-lead dating to determine that the Canyon Diablo meteorite was 4.55 billion years old.
cards.stem: How old was the Canyon Diablo meteorite found to be?
